name: Cerebral
one_liner: Online therapy and psychiatry platform with medication management, but no longer prescribes controlled substances.
short_description: Cerebral is an online mental health platform offering therapy and medication management for anxiety, depression, and insomnia, with broad insurance acceptance.
long_description: Cerebral is an online mental health company founded in 2020 that provides therapy and psychiatric medication management through video visits. The platform offers both self-pay and insurance-covered services across most US states. Following a 2022 DOJ investigation into prescribing practices, Cerebral stopped prescribing controlled substances including ADHD stimulants and benzodiazepines. The company now focuses on non-controlled psychiatric medications like SSRIs, SNRIs, and non-stimulant ADHD treatments (atomoxetine, guanfacine). Cerebral accepts major insurance plans including Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, and UnitedHealthcare, with typical copays around $30. Self-pay options include medication management at $60/month and therapy at $175/session.
best_for: Adults seeking online therapy and psychiatry for anxiety or depression

Individuals preferring combined therapy and medication on one platform
not_for: Patients needing ADHD stimulant medications (no longer prescribed)

faqs.q: Can Cerebral prescribe Adderall for ADHD?
faqs.a: No. Following a 2022 DOJ investigation, Cerebral stopped prescribing controlled substances including ADHD stimulants like Adderall and Ritalin. They only offer non-stimulant ADHD treatments like atomoxetine (Strattera) and guanfacine.
Self-pay: $60/month for medication management, $175/session for therapy, or $365/month for both. With insurance (Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, UHC), most copays are $20-50 per visit with an average of $30.
Yes, Cerebral accepts Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, and Optum in many states. They do NOT accept Medicaid or TRICARE.

faqs.q: Is Cerebral safe to use after the DOJ investigation?
faqs.a: Cerebral remains operational and HIPAA-compliant. The 2022 investigation focused on controlled substance prescribing practices, which they have since stopped. They now only prescribe non-controlled psychiatric medications.
